findings.issue: 箱 is standalone here, so it reads はこ. The rendaku reading ばこ only occurs in compounds (本箱, ゴミ箱). The kana (and consequently the romaji 'bako') gives a wrong reading of the sentence.
findings.current: てーぷでばこをとじる
findings.suggested: てーぷではこをとじる

findings.issue: Token reading for 箱 is ばこ; standalone 箱 reads はこ (rendaku ばこ appears only as second element of compounds).
Romaji carries the same wrong reading 'bako' for standalone 箱; should be 'hako'. (Separate from the known punctuation/katakana romaji issues.)

The pt gloss for 高 contains a copy-paste parenthetical claiming て-form with concessive meaning ('mesmo que seja caro' = 高くても). Here 高 is the adjective stem taking 〜そう, as the token's own note correctly states. The parenthetical teaches a wrong conjugation.

The last sentence claims 'has five hundred grams' is more natural in English — false ('is five hundred grams' is the natural English, and it is the en translation given). The remark was mirrored from the pt-BR-specific note ('tem quinhentos gramas') and only applies to Portuguese.
findings.current: In English it sounds more natural as 'has five hundred grams' than 'is five hundred grams'.
findings.suggested: In Portuguese, 'tem quinhentos gramas' sounds more natural than 'é quinhentos gramas'.

findings.issue: とても is a degree adverb meaning 'very'; the gloss 'much, a lot' suggests quantity and does not fit とても高そう ('looks very expensive'). The pt gloss 'muito' is fine; the en gloss should be 'very'.
この is strictly proximal ('this'); it never means 'that' (その/あの). The gloss 'this, that' is wrong and inconsistent with the same token glossed 'this' elsewhere in the bank.
'Of this restaurant, this cake...' is not idiomatic English for この店の中で; the natural rendering of the superlative set is 'in this store/restaurant' or 'of everything in this store'.
findings.current: Of this restaurant, this cake is the most delicious.
findings.suggested: This cake is the most delicious one in this store.
